{{short description|Family of scientific calculators by Casio}}
'''Casio V.P.A.M. calculators''' are [[scientific calculator]]s made by [[Casio]] which use Casio's [[Calculator input methods#Mathematical display|''Visually Perfect Algebraic Method'']] ('''V.P.A.M.'''), ''Natural Display'' or ''Natural V.P.A.M.'' input methods. V.P.A.M. is an [[Calculator input methods#Infix notation|infix]] system for entering mathematical expressions, used by Casio in most of its current scientific calculators. In the [[infix notation]] the [[Order of operations|precedence]] of mathematical operators is taken into account. According to Casio, in V.P.A.M. calculations can be input exactly as they are normally written. Functions, operators and symbols are shown on the calculator display and calculations are performed according to operator precedence.

==History==
The V.P.A.M. brand was first used in 1994 when the fx-991S and other scientific calculators from the "S" series were released in Japan. In 1998, the Casio fx-991W model used a two-tier (multi-line) display and the system was termed as S-V.P.A.M. (Super V.P.A.M.). The model featured a 5×6-dot LCD matrix cells on the top line of the screen and a 7-segment LCD on the bottom line of the screen that had been used in Casio fx-4500P [[programmable calculator]]s.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Casio fx-4500P: Nice looking pocket machine made in China |url=https://www.hpmuseum.org/forum/thread-3174.html |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=www.hpmuseum.org}}</ref> The S-V.P.A.M. system was also used in the other W series models and also the MS series of calculators that followed. V.P.A.M. is similar to the Direct Algebraic Logic (D.A.L.) used by [[Sharp EL-500W series|Sharp]] in some of their scientific calculators.

The fx-82ES introduced by Casio in 2004 was the first calculator to incorporate the Natural Textbook Display (or ''Natural Display'') system. It allowed the display of expressions of fractions, exponents, logarithms, powers and square roots etc. as they are written in a standard textbook.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |date=2004-04-29 |title=教科書の表記通りに数式を表示する関数電卓 |trans-title=Scientific calculator that displays mathematical formulas exactly as they appear in textbooks. |url=http://www.casio.co.jp/release/2004/fx_82es.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050403184409/http://www.casio.co.jp/release/2004/fx_82es.html |archive-date=2005-04-03 |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=www.casio.co.jp |language=ja}}</ref> ''Natural Display'' uses natural representation of mathematical expressions and formulas through a 96×31 [[dot matrix]] [[LCD]]. Casio uses the term ''Natural V.P.A.M.'' for the '''fx-ES&nbsp;Plus''' series of calculators which are the upgraded version of the fx-ES series.

In mid-2014, Casio introduced a new line of calculators called ClassWiz (stylized as C&nbsp;L&nbsp;A&nbsp;S&nbsp;S&nbsp;W&nbsp;I&nbsp;Z) for different markets, featuring a high resolution (192×63) dot matrix Natural Textbook Display and incorporating spreadsheet functions in some models.<ref name=":10" /><ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2015-06-12 |title=異様に欲しくなった電卓の話 カシオCLASSWIZ |url=https://weekly.ascii.jp/elem/000/002/633/2633536/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |website=週刊アスキー |language=ja}}</ref> This series of calculators is called the '''fx-EX''' series and it succeeds the '''fx-ES Plus''' series of calculators.

In late 2022, Casio introduced a second generation of ClassWiz line, called '''fx-CW'''. The series was originally called the fx-EZ series, but was later changed to the fx-CW series.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Admin |date=2022-02-08 |title=Etabliert im Mathematikunterricht: Die ClassWiz Serie |url=https://www.news4teachers.de/2022/02/etabliert-im-mathematikunterricht-die-classwiz-serie/ |access-date=2023-12-09 |website=News4teachers |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=iF Design - ClassWiz |url=https://ifdesign.com/en/winner-ranking/project/classwiz/564429 |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=ifdesign.com |language=en}}</ref> Calculators in this line have an updated user interface, and come with 4-gradation displays.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Casio WEW Worldwide Education Website |url=http://edu.casio.com/products/cwiz/fx991cw/ |access-date=2023-10-12 |website=Casio WEW Worldwide Education Website |language=En}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=2023-08-31 |title=操作しやすいUIを採用！カシオが使いやすさを追求したスタンダード関数電卓「ClassWiz CWシリーズ」を発売｜@DIME アットダイム |trans-title=Casio launches the "ClassWiz CW series," a standard scientific calculator designed for ease of use, featuring an easy-to-use UI! {{!}} @DIME |url=https://dime.jp/genre/1645290/ |access-date=2026-05-09 |website=@DIME アットダイム |language=ja}}</ref>

In 2025, Casio released a revised version of the fx-CW, called '''fx-CW 2nd edition''', also known as the '''fx-CW+''', or '''fx-CW II'''.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2026-01-08 |title=Introducing ClassWiz+: find out what you need to know |url=https://education.casio.co.uk/blog/introducing-classwizplus-find-out-what-you-need-to-know/ |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=Casio Calculators |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=CLASSWIZ-fx-991CN CW II_fx-999CN CW II-操作指南-CASIO |url=https://support.casio.com/global/cn/calc/manual/fx-991CNCWII_999CNCWII_cn/ |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=support.casio.com}}</ref> In markets that had not received the original fx-CW line, the series continued under the same name, fx-CW.<ref name=":5" /> This edition reintroduced several functions that had formerly been available in the fx-EX but absent from the original fx-CW.

===Natural Textbook Display===
[[File:Casio-fx115ES-5564-plainbg.jpg|thumb| Casio fx-115ES scientific calculator with [[Calculator input methods|Natural Display]]. (also called "Natural V.P.A.M." in the updated version)]]
Revised version of the MS Series including the following changes:
* Multi-line 96×31 dot matrix displays, but character cells are connected by dots like [[graphing calculator]]s
* The ability to display and edit mathematical formulas in more visual formats
* Revised design of function menu interface, formerly featured in Casio fx-4800P<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kyoro's Room Blog CASIO fx-4800P |url=http://kyoro205.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-308.html |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=kyoro205.blog.fc2.com}}</ref>
* No engineering symbol ([[SI prefixes]]) input or display facility, which was available in certain MS, W, S series models (fx-100, 115, 570 and 991MS, W, S).
* Uses the nX-U8/100 based OKI ML610901(B) microcontroller<ref>https://www.oki.com/jp/otr/2005/n203/pdf/203_R06.pdf</ref>

Model-specific features include:
* Numerical integration uses [[Gauss–Kronrod quadrature formula]]
Models:
* fx-991ES, 570ES, 115ES ''(c. 2004)''
* fx-912ES, 370ES (Japan)
* fx-500ES, 350ES, 300ES, 85ES, 83ES, 82ES<ref name=":9" /> ''(c. 2004)''
* OH-300ES (overhead projection model)
* FC-100/200V (financial functions)
* fx-5800P (Programmable)

===ClassWiz (High-resolution Natural Textbook Display)===
[[File:Fx-991EX.jpg|thumb|Casio fx-991EX ClassWiz (High-resolution Natural Textbook Display)]]
[[File:Casio fx-991DE X.JPG|thumb|Casio fx-991DE X, the German model of the fx-991EX, which contains more functions than the fx-991EX]]

====First version (X series)====
Changes to the ES Plus series include:
* Standard 192×63 display
* Icon-based mode menu formerly used on Casio fx-9700GE graphing calculators
* Mode-specific functions are accessible via a unified function key as in fx-4800P
* Now uses the nX-U16/100 based ML620Q906{{cn|date=January 2025}}
Model-specific features include:
* Scientific constants and conversion functions are grouped into categories
* Multilingual messages (excluding EX models and DE X models)
* [[QR code]] export (excluding CN X models, fx-580 VN X and fx-530AZ STUDY CAL)
* Multiline display supports up to 6 rows (excluding JP series, fx-530AZ STUDY CAL and fx-580VN X)
* Vector mode now supports maximum 4-variable vectors and 4 user-defined vector storage
* Matrix mode now supports maximum 4×4 matrices and 4 user-defined matrix storage
* New [[spreadsheet]] mode (excluding CN X and fx-580 VN X)
* Simultaneous linear equation solver supports up to 4 variables
* Polynomial equation solver supports up to 4th degree equations and inequalities
* Engineering symbols display and entry formerly found in MS, W, S, D-series calculators
* [[Periodic table]] mode with [[Relative atomic mass|atomic weight]] information (fx-JP900, fx-991CE X and fx-991RS X only)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://casio.jp/dentaku/products/fx-JP900/|title = Fx-JP900 &#124; CASIO}}</ref>
* New algorithm mode with [[Scratch (programming language)|Scratch]]-like script commands (fx-92+ Spéciale Collège only)<ref>{{Cite web |author=Ezéchiel Rencker |date=2018-11-14 |title=Autour des usages de la calculatrice en cours de mathématiques au collège - [Les nouvelles technologies pour l'enseignement des mathématiques] |url=http://revue.sesamath.net/spip.php?article1134 |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=MathémaTICE |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite patent|country=|number=JP2020035147A|title=情報処理方法、情報処理装置、およびプログラム|gdate=2020-03-05|invent1=Akiko Muraki|invent2=|invent3=|inventor1-first=|inventor2-first=|inventor3-first=|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/JP2020035147A/ja}}</ref>

====Second version (CW series)====
[[File:Casio fx-991CW.jpg|thumb|Casio fx-991CW, an international ClassWiz CW series model with built-in [[QR Code]] generation feature.]]
[[File:Fx-999CN CW.jpg|thumb|Casio fx-999CN CW, a Chinese ClassWiz CW series model, which retains the multi-statement and variable store characters function.]]
Changes to the ClassWiz X series include:<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":7" />
* The screen resolution remains at 192×63 pixels but now features 4-level grayscale display
* Cursor navigation completely replaces the previous method of using numeric keys to select menu options
* Added the Math Box application for mathematical exploration in most models
* Significant changes to the keyboard layout: the ALPHA key is removed; navigation keys for cursor movement, page flipping, returning, and confirmation (OK) are added. However, the total number of keys is reduced from 50 to 48
* Added Variable menu allows direct modification of variable values and supports storing results from the history log into variables
* Added Function menu enables the definition of two functions and their utilization across multiple applications
* Introduced CATALOG and TOOLS keys, where most functions and operations are accessed
* The M variable is removed, replaced by the z variable
* The ×10 key enters the multiplication symbol rather than the scientific notation symbol, altering calculation precedence compared to previous series
* The Statistics application now supports data sorting
* Except for CN CW models, variable store characters and multi-statement (i.e., colon ":") function are removed
* Improved calculation precision to 23 digits and increased floating-point precision to 60 bits
* The shutdown screen now includes the Casio logo and Casio Education Statement slogan, Boost your Curiosity.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Global Trends in Education—What Are 21st Century Skills? |url=http://edu.casio.com/brand_statement/ |access-date=2023-12-09 |website=Casio WEW Worldwide Education Website |language=ja}}</ref> On the CN CW series, this slogan is additionally presented in Chinese as "激发你的好奇心"
* Now uses the nX-U16/100 based ML620Q909 with built-in BCD coprocessor{{cn|date=January 2025}}
* The sliding protective cover is replaced with a snap-on cover

Model-specific features include:
* The previous Verify mode is no longer a standalone mode but dispersed across multiple modes, accessible within the Calculate, Complex, Table, and Equation applications
* The CALC function, present in most earlier models, has been removed from the majority of models except for the fx-880BTG and JP CW series
* The SOLVE function becomes a part of the Equation application
* When solving cubic equations, the capability to find local maximum and minimum values is supported
* Periodic table mode with atomic weight information (fx-JP900CW and fx-880BTG only)

====Revision of second version (CW 2nd edition series)====
[[File:Fx-9910CW 2nd edition.jpg|alt=Casio fx-9910CW 2nd edition with CATALOG List menu opened|thumb|Casio fx-9910CW 2nd edition, as the first model in the fx-CW 2nd edition series, is released for the North American market]]
Key differences from the CW series include:<ref>{{Cite web |title=CLASSWIZ-fx-9910CW (2nd edition)-Manuals-CASIO |url=https://support.casio.com/global/en/calc/manual/fx-9910CW_en/ |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=support.casio.com}}</ref>

* Menu items can now be selected using number keys or symbol keys, such as plus (+), minus (−), multiply (×), divide (÷), and others
* The FORMAT button defaults to the same function as the former S<>D key, toggling between Standard and Decimal display formats
* The ×10 key defaults to scientific notation and automatically inserts brackets during calculations
* A new CATALOG List menu was introduced, displaying all functions and symbols in one menu
* Some typos in the messages have been corrected
* Navigation keys changed from engraved to printed labels, and the OFF label is highlighted in reverse colour
Model-specific features include:

* The order of the apps icon on the home screen varies depending on the model
